To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
resampling-based empirical-Bayes FDR-controlling procedures provide a powerful alternative to the classical and linear step-up FDR-controlling multiple testing methods.
the proposed resampling-based empirical Bayesian approach provides a powerful alternative to existing FDR controlling methods.

the proposed empirical Bayes multiple test procedures are competitive with or superior to the linear step-up procedure of Storey and Tibishirani, and the proposed procedures provide an alternative to existing methods for controlling a broad range of error rates, including error rates based on functions of V(n) and S(n) other than the proportion of false discoveries.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing a new class of multiple testing procedures that can control a broad class of error rates.
a new class of resampling-based empirical Bayesian multiple testing procedures that offer Type I error control in a broad class of testing situations.
the development of multiple testing procedures that control Type I error rates that are more general than the family-wise error rate and false discovery rate.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the empirical Bayes procedure performs as well as, and sometimes better than, the linear step-up procedure in terms of Type I error and FDR control, with a potential for improved power, and that the empirical Bayest procedure is more generally applicable than the linear step-up approach, in the sense of being applicable to general data generating distributions and arbitrary dependence structures.
resampling-based empirical Bayesian procedures are a promising approach to FDR-controlling multiple testing, and should be considered in conjunction with the classical and linear step-up procedures.
the empirical Bayes procedure performs well under a wide variety of scenarios and is competitive with or outperforms the linear step-up procedure in terms of Type I error rate control and power.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed resampling-based empirical Bayesian procedures provide a new approach for multiple testing that can be competitive with or superior to existing methods.
the proposed procedures provide a new approach for controlling a broad range of error rates in the multiple testing problem.

we provide a new approach for controlling a general class of Type I errors in multiple hypothesis testing, and that this new approach is competitive with or outperforms widely-used linear step-up procedures.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the resampling-based approach is more flexible and more powerful than the classical approach, while maintaining control of the FDR.
the proposed procedures offer an appealing alternative to the Storey and Benjamini-Hochberg approaches for controlling the FDR, and more generally, the gTP and gEV error rates.

the resampling-based approach can provide a powerful alternative to existing methods for controlling the FDR, especially when the dependence structure of variables is not known a priori and/or when the data generating distribution is unknown.
